atoms.b: Burns wrote a lot of poems called ballads. One important feature of a ((++ballad play)) is that the last word of the 2nd and 4th lines rhyme.
These ballads weren’t just about ((++ordinary frightening)) things, Burns also liked to write about love. Burns himself was married and had ((++12 200)) children!

instruction.text: Listen to the poem and select the underlined word

end.text:
Although they are two different languages, lots of the words in Scots and English are similar, even if they are spelt slightly differently.

For example: luve - love
end.sound: Although they are two different languages, lots of the words in Scots and English are similar, even if they are spelt slightly differently.

atoms.a: O my love is like a red red rose that’s newly sprung in June; O my love is like the melody that’s sweetly played in tune.
What two words in the poem rhyme?

hint.text: Two words rhyme if they sound the same at the end.

atoms.a: What lines are the words “June” and “tune” on?
The poem A Red, Red Rose is a ballad.
atoms.sound: The poem 'A Red Red Rose' is a ballad.

hint.text: Remember, most ballads have rhyming words at the end of the 2nd and 4th lines.

instruction.text: Burns also used his poetry to talk about his love for Scotland. Complete the rhyme in this poem.

trainers.hint: You are looking for the word that rhymes with “sake”.

atoms.a: That I for poor auld Scotland’s sake
atoms.sound: That I for poor auld Scotland’s sayk, some useful plan or book could

instruction.text: Look at the completed rhyme. What do you think Burns is saying?

b: ++I want to write something for Scotland.
I am proud to be Welsh.

end.text: One of Burns’ most famous poems is called Auld Lang Syne. Every year, lots of people sing this on New Year’s Eve.
end.sound: One of Burns’s most famous poems is called Auld Lang Syne. Every year, lots of people sing this on New Year’s Eve.

instruction.text: Look at these lines of the poem. What English word do you think “auld” sounds like?

feedback.end: In English, the words “for auld lang syne” mean “for old long since”.

atoms.a: For auld lang syne my jo, for auld lang syne. We’ll tak a cuppakindness yet, for auld lang syne.

instruction.text: “For old long since” doesn’t quite make sense in English. What do you think would be a better translation?

feedback.end: The poem talks about remembering the past. People sing it on New Year’s Eve every year as a way to say goodbye to the year that has just gone.
